visuals.title: Where it strikes
visuals.text: Usually one joint, most often the knee. Watch for spread in the blood and sepsis.

visuals.title: Kocher's criteria in a limping child

visual.label: 3 points: 93%
visual.caption: Each criterion scores 1; 3 or more makes septic arthritis very likely.

facts.label: Gram stain negative, so culture anyway

visuals.title: Order of actions
nodes: IV flucloxacillin (vancomycin if MRSA or allergy)

glossary.Joint space: The fluid-filled cavity between the bones of a joint.
glossary.Prosthetic joint: An artificial joint replacement, such as a hip or knee.
glossary.Immunosuppression: Weakened immune defences from drugs or disease.
glossary.Rheumatoid arthritis: An autoimmune inflammatory arthritis; damaged joints are easier to infect.
glossary.Steroids: Glucocorticoid drugs such as prednisolone that suppress immunity.
glossary.Weight-bear: Put weight through a leg when standing or walking.
glossary.Range of movement: How far a joint can move in each direction.
glossary.Limping: Walking unevenly to avoid putting weight on a painful leg.
glossary.Probability: How likely something is, as a percentage.
glossary.IV drug use: Injecting drugs into a vein, which can carry bacteria into the blood.
glossary.Streptococcus: A group of Gram-positive bacteria causing throat, skin and joint infections.
glossary.Soft tissue infection: Infection of skin, fat or muscle, such as cellulitis.
glossary.Sexually active: Having sex, so at risk of sexually transmitted infections.
glossary.Gold standard: The best available test against which others are judged.
glossary.Culture: Growing bacteria from a sample to identify them and test antibiotics.
glossary.Neutrophils: The commonest white blood cells; they dominate infected fluid.
glossary.Orthopaedic: Relating to the surgical specialty of bones and joints.
glossary.Empiric: Started before the organism is known, aimed at the likeliest cause.
glossary.Penicillin allergy: An immune reaction to penicillins; flucloxacillin is one.
glossary.Drainage: Letting pus or fluid out of a space.
glossary.Serial aspirations: Repeated drawing off of joint fluid with a needle over days.
glossary.Medical emergency: A condition needing immediate treatment to prevent death or lasting harm.
glossary.Immobilisation: Keeping the joint still to rest it.
glossary.Proliferation: Rapid multiplication of cells or organisms.
glossary.Proteolytic enzymes: Enzymes that break down proteins, here destroying cartilage.
glossary.Articular cartilage: The smooth cartilage covering bone ends in a joint.
glossary.Implant: A man-made device placed in the body.
glossary.Pretest probability: How likely a disease is before the test result is known.
glossary.Systemic inflammatory response: Whole-body reaction to infection: fever, raised WCC and ESR.
glossary.Disseminated gonococcal infection: Gonorrhoea that has spread through the blood to joints, tendons and skin.
glossary.Migratory: Moving from one joint to another over time.
glossary.Dermatitis: Inflammation of the skin; here small pustules or spots.
glossary.Sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.Contiguous spread: Infection spreading directly from a neighbouring structure.
